above- and belowground insect herbivores can facilitate each others' feeding by altering plant responses to herbivory.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the aphid facilitates root herbivory and vice versa, but that the aphid also benefits the root herbivores by inducing a compensatory growth response in the host plant.

the aphids and weevils are both facilitative to each other, with aphids inducing a compensatory growth response in the plant and weevils causing the plant to abandon compensatory growth in favour of tolerance.
the aphids benefit from compensatory growth and the vine weevils from the lack of it.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the aphids and vine weevil larvae facilitate each other’s feeding by altering the plant’s response to herbivory.
the aphids induce plant resistance/tolerance, and this is then overridden by the vine weevil larvae.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the aphid and vine weevil are not competing with each other, but instead, the aphid facilitates the feeding of the vine weevil, which in turn facilitates feeding of the aphid.
positive interactions between insect herbives can occur, even between those with contrasting feeding modes.
